hero.headline: Justice Department moves to strip citizenship from 17 naturalized Americans
hero.body:
The Justice Department has filed denaturalization proceedings against 17 naturalized US citizens, representing a significant expansion of citizenship revocation efforts under the Trump administration. The move follows a June 11 memo directing federal attorneys to prioritize denaturalization cases against people who either "illegally procured" citizenship or obtained it through "concealment of a material fact or by willful misrepresentation."

The policy targets naturalized citizens across multiple priority categories, including those involved in war crimes, human rights abuses, and criminal activity. According to the memo, denaturalization efforts should focus on naturalized criminals, gang members, and individuals convicted of crimes who pose ongoing threats to the country. The directive also expands the scope to include cases involving false statements on immigration forms, financial fraud, and medical fraud.

Denaturalization is a rare legal process that allows the government to revoke citizenship from naturalized Americans. Unlike deportation proceedings for non-citizens, denaturalization requires federal court review. The government must prove that citizenship was obtained illegally or fraudulently. If successful, the proceedings would strip individuals of their US citizenship and could lead to deportation.

One case already concluded involved Elliott Duke, a military veteran originally from the UK who was convicted of distributing child sexual abuse material. A judge ordered revocation of his citizenship on June 13 after he failed to disclose the conviction during naturalization.

The policy has raised concerns among immigration advocates. Sameera Hafiz, policy director of the Immigration Legal Resource Center, told NPR: "It is kind of, in a way, trying to create a second class of US citizens." Civil rights attorneys note that denaturalization through civil litigation strips individuals of certain protections available in criminal cases, including the right to a government-provided attorney and a higher standard of proof. The civil process lowers the evidentiary threshold and speeds up proceedings.

The memo's focus on denaturalization reflects broader changes within the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division. The division, traditionally tasked with combating racial discrimination, has been redirected toward the Trump administration's policy priorities, including efforts to end diversity, equity, and inclusion programs. According to NPR, approximately 250 attorneys, or 70 percent of the division's lawyers, left the department between January and May.

The estimated 25 million US citizens who immigrated to the country represent the broader population potentially affected by the administration's approach. Each denaturalization case will proceed independently through federal court, where judges will evaluate whether the government has met its burden of proof. The individuals targeted retain the right to legal representation and can contest the allegations in court.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Jump as Iran and Israel Exchange Strikes
cards.teaser: Oil markets rallied after military hostilities between Iran and Israel raised concerns about Middle East stability.
cards.body:
Oil prices surged after Iran and Israel exchanged military strikes, raising concerns about the stability of the Middle East ceasefire. The volatility in energy markets reflected worries about the security of oil supplies from the region, which is critical to global energy chains.

Following Iran's announcement that it had halted its military operations, oil prices eased. Israel's Prime Minister said his country was holding fire "at the moment," though both sides warned of potential retaliation if the ceasefire were breached again. Stock markets, which initially fell on the escalation, recovered some losses as tensions appeared to stabilize.

cards.headline: Energy-Importing Countries Shift to Domestic Production Amid Iran War
cards.teaser: Nations dependent on imported energy are prioritizing domestic sources to shield themselves from volatile global markets.
cards.body:
Countries that rely heavily on energy imports are turning inward to protect their economies from oil and natural gas price volatility caused by the Iran conflict. The strategic shift reflects growing concerns about supply security as Middle East tensions disrupt traditional energy trade patterns.

Governments are accelerating investments in domestic energy production and alternative sources to reduce dependence on imports. The trend marks a significant change in energy policy for nations that have historically relied on global markets for their fuel needs.

cards.headline: Inflation Expected to Exceed 4 Percent, Testing New Fed Chair
cards.teaser: Bond markets are watching to see how Fed Chair Warsh responds as inflation heads toward a three-year high.
cards.body:
Inflation is projected to surpass 4 percent this week when new data is released, marking a three-year high and presenting Fed Chair Warsh with his biggest test since taking office. Bond traders are betting on a surge in the Consumer Price Index that could force the Federal Reserve to reconsider its monetary policy stance.

The bond market is looking for signals that Warsh will take aggressive action to combat rising prices. The inflation spike comes amid broader economic uncertainty, including volatile energy prices and continued strength in consumer spending that has kept upward pressure on costs.

cards.headline: Trump formally nominates Todd Blanche for attorney general
cards.teaser: The president submitted his former personal lawyer's nomination amid questions about a Justice Department fund.
cards.body:
President Trump nominated Todd Blanche to serve as attorney general on Monday. Blanche, Trump's former personal lawyer, has been acting in the role since April, following Trump's dismissal of Pam Bondi from the position.

The nomination draws criticism from Democrats. Senator Adam Schiff called for the Senate to "vigorously oppose" the appointment, arguing that Blanche "has been unable to put aside his role as Donald Trump's criminal defense lawyer and represent the American people instead." Blanche now faces Senate Judiciary Committee review and requires Senate confirmation to permanently lead the Justice Department.

cards.headline: Airlines Cut 2026 Profit Forecast in Half as Fuel Costs Surge
cards.teaser: Global airlines slashed their profit projections by nearly 50 percent after fuel costs jumped by $100 billion.
cards.body:
US carriers spent $6.5 billion on fuel in April as jet fuel prices surged globally due to the Iran conflict. The International Air Transport Association responded by cutting its 2026 profit forecast for the airline industry nearly in half.

The spike in fuel costs represents a major shock to aviation economics. Industry leaders gathered at a summit in Rio to address the crisis, while airplane engine manufacturers faced scrutiny over their pricing during the fuel emergency.

cards.headline: Microsoft shuts down GitHub repositories after password theft hack
cards.teaser: Microsoft closed dozens of GitHub code repositories for Azure and AI tools after a hack targeted developer passwords.
cards.body:
Microsoft took down dozens of GitHub repositories containing open source code for its Azure and artificial intelligence development tools following a reported security breach. The hack targeted passwords of developers working with the tools, prompting the emergency shutdown.

The affected repositories included coding tools used by developers building applications on Microsoft's cloud platform and AI services. Microsoft has not disclosed how many developers were affected or when the repositories will be restored.

cards.headline: Flesh-eating cattle parasite detected outside Texas
cards.teaser: New screwworm cases have been confirmed beyond Texas, expanding the range of the destructive livestock pest.
cards.body:
Agricultural officials have confirmed three additional cases of New World screwworm in livestock. The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service reported two cases in Texas—affecting a calf in La Salle County and a goat in Gillespie County—and one case in New Mexico.

Screwworm larvae feed on living tissue of warm-blooded animals, creating wounds that can prove fatal if left untreated. The parasite was eradicated from the United States decades ago but has occasionally reappeared near the southern border. The recent expansion beyond Texas marks a significant development as officials work to contain the parasite's spread.

cards.headline: Kennedy Center removes Trump name from website after court order
cards.teaser: The arts venue removed Trump branding from its website following a judicial ruling.
cards.body:
A US district judge ordered the Kennedy Center to remove President Trump's name from its website, and the performing arts venue complied by taking down references to a "Trump Kennedy Center" on Monday.

The removal came ahead of a June 12 deadline set by the center's general counsel for all references to the president to be removed from its materials.

cards.headline: Pentagon revises military religious classification list
cards.teaser: The Defense Department updated its list of recognized religious affiliations following pushback from Utah lawmakers.
cards.body:
The Pentagon updated its list of recognized religious affiliations following pressure from Utah lawmakers. The Defense Department had released a revised version of the list four months earlier but quickly withdrew it without explanation.

The controversy involved how the Defense Department categorized religious groups in its official records. Utah Republicans and religious organizations objected to the changes, prompting the Pentagon to reconsider its classification system. The list determines how service members can identify their faith in military databases.

cards.headline: Defense rests in trial of teen charged in fatal track meet stabbing
cards.teaser: The defense concluded its case without calling the accused to testify in the murder trial stemming from a high school track meet death.
cards.body:
The defense rested its case in the murder trial of Karmelo Anthony, a teenager charged in the fatal stabbing of Austin Metcalf at a track meet in Frisco. Anthony did not take the stand to testify in his own defense.

Witnesses testified that Anthony appeared distraught after the stabbing incident. Eyewitnesses at the track meet described the confrontation that led to the fatal stabbing. The case has drawn attention as it involves violence at a high school athletic event. The trial will now move toward closing arguments and jury deliberations.

cards.headline: Apple unveils AI updates at developers conference
cards.teaser: The company announced new artificial intelligence features while emphasizing security and child safety measures.
cards.body:
Apple introduced significant AI updates at its annual developers conference, with a major focus on a redesigned Siri. The announcements emphasized privacy protections and new child safety features, addressing concerns about harmful applications like "nudification" apps. Apple positioned its AI approach as distinct from competitors, with executives critiquing other companies' implementations during the presentation.

To support broader developer participation in AI, Apple waived cloud API costs for developers whose apps have fewer than 2 million first-time downloads on the App Store. This move comes as AI development costs continue to rise across the industry.

cards.headline: California governor primary vote counting continues
cards.teaser: Updated tallies show county-by-county results as ballot counting extends beyond election day.
cards.body:
California election officials continue counting ballots from the 2026 gubernatorial primary, with updated results showing how each county voted. Democrat Xavier Becerra has pulled ahead in the race as additional votes are tallied.

The extended counting timeline reflects California's vote-by-mail system and verification procedures. Ballots postmarked by election day are still being processed and added to totals. NBC News and other outlets are tracking live results as counties report updated figures. The prolonged counting process has renewed discussion about ballot processing timelines in the state.

hero.headline: OpenAI Files Confidentially for IPO in Test of Investor Appetite for AI
hero.body:
OpenAI has confidentially submitted a Form S-1 to the US Securities and Exchange Commission, marking the beginning of its journey toward a public listing. The filing comes roughly a week after rival Anthropic, maker of the Claude chatbot, made a similar confidential submission.

In a Monday blog post, OpenAI acknowledged the filing and stated that it expects details to eventually become public. "We recently submitted a confidential S-1. We expect it to leak so we're just announcing it," the company wrote. The ChatGPT maker is expected to be valued at more than $850 billion.

OpenAI emphasized that it has not yet decided on timing for the actual IPO launch. "We have not decided on timing yet; it may be a while because there are things we want to do that are likely easier as a private company. But it's a complicated set of tradeoffs and this gives us the option to go public sooner if that ends up being best," the company stated.

The confidential filing process allows companies to begin preparing for an IPO while keeping detailed financial information private until closer to their public debut. This preliminary step gives OpenAI flexibility as it weighs the benefits and drawbacks of remaining private versus going public.

The filing intensifies competition between the two leading AI companies. Both firms have been racing toward public markets for roughly a year, with Anthropic filing first on June 1st. Wall Street banks are closely monitoring both companies as they position themselves to capture underwriting fees and offer shares to institutional clients.

OpenAI's decision to publicly announce its confidential filing, rather than keeping it private, suggests the company wanted to control its own narrative. The company acknowledged that such filings typically become public knowledge eventually, so it chose to communicate the news directly to stakeholders.

The timing reflects broader trends in the AI industry. As artificial intelligence technology matures and competition intensifies, private AI companies face mounting pressure to provide investors with liquidity. OpenAI has raised billions in venture capital funding in recent years, reaching a valuation that made it one of the most valuable private technology companies globally.

The move also signals confidence in investor appetite for AI companies, despite recent volatility in technology stocks. The company's eventual public offering will subject it to greater financial scrutiny and mandatory quarterly reporting requirements that private companies typically avoid.

The path from confidential filing to actual trading typically spans several months. OpenAI will eventually need to publicly release detailed financial statements and risk disclosures before conducting a roadshow to pitch institutional investors. Potential shareholders will examine the company's revenue growth, profitability prospects, and competitive positioning against both established technology giants and other AI-focused startups.

cards.headline: Airlines Cut 2026 Profit Forecast in Half as Fuel Costs Surge
cards.teaser: Global airlines slashed their profit projections by nearly 50 percent after fuel costs jumped by $100 billion.
cards.body:
US carriers spent $6.5 billion on fuel in April as jet fuel prices surged globally due to the Iran conflict. The International Air Transport Association responded by cutting its 2026 profit forecast for the airline industry nearly in half.

The spike in fuel costs represents a major shock to aviation economics. Industry leaders gathered at a summit in Rio to address the crisis, while airplane engine manufacturers faced scrutiny over their pricing during the fuel emergency.

cards.teaser: Oil markets rallied after military hostilities between Iran and Israel raised concerns about Middle East stability.
cards.body:

Following Iran's announcement that it had halted its military operations, oil prices eased. Israel's Prime Minister said his country was holding fire "at the moment," though both sides warned of potential retaliation if the ceasefire were breached again. Stock markets, which initially fell on the escalation, recovered some losses as tensions appeared to stabilize.

Governments are accelerating investments in domestic energy production and alternative sources to reduce dependence on imports. The trend marks a significant change in energy policy for nations that have historically relied on global markets for their fuel needs.

cards.headline: Banks Use SpaceX IPO to Attract Wealthy Clients
cards.teaser: Wall Street firms are offering their richest customers early access to the SpaceX public listing.
cards.body:
Major banks are giving their wealthiest clients special access to this week's SpaceX initial public offering, using the high-profile deal to strengthen relationships in their wealth management divisions. The strategy reflects the growing importance of serving ultra-high-net-worth individuals as a profit center for financial institutions.

The velvet rope treatment for the SpaceX IPO allows private wealth clients to secure shares before the general public, a perk that banks use to differentiate their services. Wealth management has become an increasingly competitive business for Wall Street as banks seek stable revenue sources beyond volatile trading operations.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Rally as Tech Stocks Recover from Sell-Off
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 closed higher as chip stocks rebounded and geopolitical tensions showed signs of easing.
cards.body:
The S&P 500 finished higher as semiconductor stocks staged a comeback following a three-day decline. The Nasdaq snapped its losing streak as major technology names including Marvell, Intel, and Micron led the recovery. Iran's announcement that it had stopped strikes on Israel helped ease investor concerns about escalating conflict.

The Dow ended lower despite the broader market gains, reflecting mixed sector performance. Oil prices rose during the session before paring gains as Middle East tensions appeared to stabilize. Technology stocks had faced selling pressure in recent sessions amid fears about artificial intelligence valuations and broader market volatility.

hero.headline: OpenAI files confidentially for public offering
hero.body:
OpenAI has filed confidentially to go public on the US stock market, the company announced Monday. The ChatGPT maker is expected to be valued at more than $850 billion.

In a blog post, OpenAI stated: "We recently submitted a confidential S-1. We expect it to leak so we're just announcing it. We have not decided on timing yet; it may be a while because there are things we want to do that are likely easier as a private company. But it's a complicated set of tradeoffs and this gives us the option to go public sooner if that ends up being best."

An S-1 is an investor prospectus that companies submit to the Securities and Exchange Commission ahead of an initial public offering. The confidential filing process allows firms to submit their IPO paperwork to regulators without immediately revealing financial details to the public.

The move comes just over a week after Anthropic, OpenAI's main rival and maker of the Claude chatbot, announced its own confidential IPO filing with the SEC. The near-simultaneous filings from the two leading artificial intelligence companies intensify the competitive race between them to reach the public markets.

OpenAI has raised billions in venture funding from investors including Microsoft, while Anthropic has secured substantial backing from Google and other investors. Both companies are now pursuing paths that will subject them to quarterly earnings reports and shareholder oversight once they become publicly traded entities.

The timing reflects growing investor appetite for artificial intelligence companies as the technology gains wider adoption across industries. Both firms will need to demonstrate sustainable business models and revenue growth to justify their valuations as they transition from private operations to public market scrutiny.

OpenAI's announcement that it expects its filing to become public underscores the practical reality that confidential submissions often leak before companies are ready for full disclosure. By announcing the filing themselves, the company controlled the narrative around the announcement rather than waiting for information to emerge through other channels.

The confidential filing process typically extends over several months as regulators review submissions and companies prepare for roadshows to pitch their offerings to institutional investors. The SEC's review period gives both companies time to make adjustments to their financial disclosures before they formally proceed with a public offering.

Neither company has provided a specific timeline for when their shares might begin trading. OpenAI indicated that the decision to go public depends on weighing various factors, suggesting the company wants to remain private for the near term if certain strategic objectives are easier to accomplish outside the public market structure. The competition between the two AI firms to complete their offerings could influence how the market receives both debuts.

cards.headline: Apple unveils macOS 27 Golden Gate with AI-powered Siri
cards.teaser: Apple introduced macOS 27 Golden Gate at its developer conference, featuring upgraded Siri AI capabilities and interface refinements.
cards.body:
Apple unveiled macOS 27 Golden Gate at its Worldwide Developers Conference, featuring an AI-powered redesign of Siri and updates to the Liquid Glass interface. The new Siri assistant represents a significant upgrade to the company's longstanding virtual assistant, with AI at the center of the improvements.

The operating system will exclusively support Apple Silicon Macs with M1 chips or newer, discontinuing compatibility with Intel-based machines. This marks another milestone in Apple's ongoing transition away from Intel processors.

cards.headline: macOS 27 ends support for Intel Macs
cards.teaser: Apple's next macOS release will require an M1 chip or newer, dropping all Intel-based Mac computers from compatibility.
cards.body:
Apple has announced that macOS 27, called Golden Gate, will exclusively support Apple Silicon Macs with M1 chips or newer. This marks the end of software compatibility for Intel-based Mac computers that the company sold before and during its transition to custom processors.

Intel Mac users will no longer receive operating system updates, security patches for the new OS, or access to macOS 27's new features, including enhanced Siri AI tools. The move represents Apple's complete shift away from Intel hardware support as it finalizes its transition to proprietary chip designs.

cards.headline: iOS 27 maintains support for older iPhones
cards.teaser: Apple's iOS 27 will not drop any iPhone models from compatibility, while only a few older iPad models lose support.
cards.body:
Apple is keeping iOS 27 compatible with all currently supported iPhone models, allowing older device owners to receive the latest software updates. This approach represents a shift from Apple's typical practice of discontinuing support for the oldest devices with each major iOS release.

iPadOS 27 will drop support for a small number of older iPad models. Meanwhile, Apple is being more aggressive with other product lines—watchOS 27 and tvOS 27 are cutting support for multiple older device generations, including at least three Apple Watch generations and two Apple TV models.

cards.headline: Apple waives cloud AI costs for small developers
cards.teaser: Apple will not charge cloud API fees to developers whose apps have fewer than 2 million first-time downloads on the App Store.
cards.body:
Apple is eliminating cloud-based AI API costs for developers whose apps have attracted fewer than 2 million first-time downloads on the App Store. The initiative addresses rising expenses associated with integrating artificial intelligence into mobile applications.

The move comes as AI development increasingly requires substantial computing resources, making experimentation costly for independent creators and small teams. By removing these financial barriers, Apple aims to encourage broader adoption of AI features across its developer ecosystem.

cards.headline: Waymo acquires former Apple self-driving car facility for $220 million
cards.teaser: Waymo purchased a 5,500-acre Arizona testing facility that was owned by a company linked to Apple's discontinued autonomous vehicle program.
cards.body:
Waymo has purchased a 5,500-acre proving ground in Arizona for $220 million from Route 14 Investment Partners LLC, a Delaware company linked to Apple. County records confirm the transaction was completed for the sprawling facility that Apple previously used to develop its autonomous vehicle technology.

The acquisition gives Waymo a substantial new space to conduct testing and advancement of its self-driving car platform. Apple had invested considerable resources into its car project before ultimately shutting down the initiative, leaving the Arizona site available for purchase.

cards.headline: Meta accuses NSO Group of violating spyware injunction
cards.teaser: Meta asked a court to hold NSO Group in contempt, claiming the spyware company violated an injunction with new WhatsApp attacks.
cards.body:
Meta filed court documents alleging NSO Group violated a previous injunction by conducting new attacks targeting WhatsApp users. The company said it disrupted spear phishing attempts and is asking the court to hold NSO in contempt of the existing order.

NSO Group, which sells surveillance software to governments, has been subject to legal restrictions following earlier litigation. Meta claims the new attacks represent a breach of those court-ordered limits on NSO's activities targeting its messaging platform.

hero.headline: Knicks defeat Spurs in Game 2 to take 2-0 lead in NBA Finals
hero.body:
The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs in Game 2 of the NBA Finals, extending their dominance in the best-of-seven series. The Knicks are now three wins away from capturing their first championship since 1973.

The Knicks arrived at the Finals riding an 11-game winning streak, having demolished opponents throughout the playoffs. They faced the Spurs, who had eliminated the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder in the previous round. The Spurs are led by Victor Wembanyama, widely considered the most exciting player in the league.

Despite the formidable opponent, the Knicks prevailed. Jalen Brunson delivered a dominant performance, scoring 30 points with 13 coming in the fourth quarter. When asked how his team managed to pull away, Brunson emphasized team resilience. "Just sticking together, it wasn't really our night and wasn't really my night most of the night but we kept finding a way, kept chipping away," he said. "Just knowing we have each other's back, there's a lot of things we could have done better, but I think our togetherness was really the biggest difference."

OG Anunoby also stepped up in crucial moments, scoring 12 of his 17 points in the fourth quarter. The Knicks showed impressive discipline down the stretch, recording no turnovers in the final quarter while the Spurs committed five turnovers and shot just 28.6%.

Wembanyama led San Antonio with 26 points and 12 rebounds but struggled with his shot efficiency, making just 6 of 21 attempts. He briefly limped off the court in the third quarter before returning. After the game, Wembanyama acknowledged his poor performance without making excuses. "I was bad tonight, it's not more complicated than that," he said, denying that nerves affected the team's play.

The series will now shift to Madison Square Garden for Game 3, marking the first NBA Finals game in New York in 27 years. The return of the Finals to the city has generated enormous excitement and economic impact. The championship run has drawn international fans eager to witness the Knicks' pursuit of a historic title.

Enhanced security measures will be implemented for the MSG games, with President Trump planning to attend Game 3. The NYPD announced it would cancel a watch party outside the arena as part of security precautions. The Knicks are urging fans to arrive at least two hours before tipoff.

Ticket prices have reached historic levels, with a winning auction bid for two celebrity row seats at Game 3 reaching one million dollars. The playoff run has electrified New York City, with supporters recognizing they are witnessing something special in franchise history.

cards.headline: Chiefs sign cornerback L'Jarius Sneed to one-year contract
cards.teaser: The Kansas City Chiefs have signed veteran cornerback L'Jarius Sneed to a one-year deal worth up to $5 million.
cards.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs have reunited with cornerback L'Jarius Sneed, signing him to a one-year contract worth up to $5 million. Sneed previously won two Super Bowl championships with Kansas City before departing the franchise.

The signing comes after Chiefs cornerback Jaylen Watson recruited Sneed while both were with the Rams. Sneed's return adds veteran depth to the Kansas City secondary as the team prepares for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: 76ers promote Mike Gansey to president, Jameer Nelson to executive VP
cards.teaser: The Philadelphia 76ers have named Mike Gansey as team president and promoted Jameer Nelson to executive vice president of basketball operations.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers have restructured their front office, promoting Mike Gansey to president and Jameer Nelson to executive vice president of basketball operations. Gansey, who previously worked under former general manager Bob Myers, will now lead the organization's basketball operations.

Gansey stated he plans to build around the Sixers' current core while developing the team's organizational culture. He emphasized wanting to cultivate positive contributors within the franchise. Nelson, a former NBA player, moves into an expanded executive role as the team seeks a path toward an NBA championship.

cards.headline: Somali referee Omar Artan dropped from World Cup after US denies entry
cards.teaser: Omar Artan, who was set to become the first Somalian to referee at the World Cup finals, has been removed from the officials list after being denied entry to the United States.
cards.body:
Omar Artan, a top African referee from Somalia, has been dropped from the World Cup after being denied entry to the United States. He was set to make history as the first Somali official to referee at the tournament.

Artan was reportedly refused entry at Miami International Airport despite holding a valid travel visa. His exclusion removes one of FIFA's selected officials from the competition, which will be co-hosted by the United States, Mexico, and Canada.

cards.headline: Netherlands' Jurrien Timber ruled out of World Cup with groin injury
cards.teaser: Arsenal defender Jurrien Timber has been ruled out of the Netherlands' World Cup campaign due to a groin injury.
cards.body:
Arsenal defender Jurrien Timber has been ruled out of the Netherlands' World Cup campaign due to a groin injury. The starting defender will not be available as the team prepares for their opening matches.

Meanwhile, Brazil's Neymar is making good progress in his recovery from injury as teams finalize their rosters ahead of the tournament.

cards.headline: England's Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson under investigation for nightclub incident
cards.teaser: England cricket captain Ben Stokes and pace bowler Gus Atkinson are being investigated by the England and Wales Cricket Board over a nightclub incident.
cards.body:
The England and Wales Cricket Board is investigating an incident involving England cricket captain Ben Stokes and pace bowler Gus Atkinson at a nightclub. A Saracens academy player was also involved in the matter.

Saracens, the Premiership Rugby club, is conducting a separate investigation into the incident alongside cricket authorities.

cards.headline: Big 12 teams consider boycotting Texas Tech over Brendan Sorsby ruling
cards.teaser: Big 12 conference teams are considering not playing Texas Tech after a Texas judge ruled that quarterback Brendan Sorsby can play despite a gambling investigation.
cards.body:
Multiple Big 12 conference teams are considering refusing to play Texas Tech following a judge's decision to grant quarterback Brendan Sorsby eligibility for the 2026 season. Sorsby won an injunction against the NCAA despite admitting to gambling violations during an ongoing probe.

Coaches and athletic directors across college athletics expressed anger at the ruling, with some describing themselves as disgusted and stunned by the decision. The controversy has raised questions about the integrity of college sports enforcement, with critics arguing that allowing Sorsby to play undermines NCAA rules and competitive fairness.

hero.headline: Former Justice Department Attorneys Criticize Live Nation-Ticketmaster Settlement
hero.body:
Two former senior antitrust attorneys at the U.S. Department of Justice criticized the department's surprise settlement with Live Nation and Ticketmaster, calling it deeply troubling selective non-prosecution of political allies. The settlement was reached just one week after trial began in a major antitrust case brought by the DOJ and over 30 states against the company.

The former attorneys, who were instrumental in building the case against Live Nation and Ticketmaster, expressed serious concerns about the abrupt resolution. They questioned the timing and terms of the deal, suggesting it raised troubling questions about how the department handled this high-profile enforcement action.

The original lawsuit represented one of the most significant antitrust cases in the entertainment industry in recent years. The DOJ and attorneys general from 30 states, including California, Massachusetts, Utah and Wyoming, accused Live Nation of monopolistic practices that dominated the live entertainment and ticketing markets. New York's attorney general told jurors that Ticketmaster keeps an average of $7.58 from each ticket sold at major concert venues, claiming the company harms artists, venues and fans through its market dominance.

Under the settlement agreement, Live Nation will establish a $280 million fund for participating states. Ticketmaster must open parts of its ticketing platform to rival companies and divest from exclusive booking agreements with 13 U.S. amphitheaters. The deal also caps Ticketmaster service fees at 15 percent of the ticket price and limits long-term exclusivity contracts with venues.

In a statement, Live Nation CEO Michael Rapino said the settlement represented progress for the concert industry. "By giving artists greater flexibility in choosing their promotional partners and ticketing strategy while also keeping the cost of a concert more affordable for fans, we are putting more power where it should be with artists and fans," he said.

However, the settlement has faced significant pushback. A bipartisan group of state attorneys general refused to accept the terms, arguing the deal fails to address Live Nation's core monopoly in ticketing. Letitia James, New York's attorney general, stated that the settlement would benefit Live Nation at consumers' expense and does not rectify the company's dominance.

"The settlement recently announced with the U.S. Department of Justice fails to address the monopoly at the center of this case," James said. "My attorney general colleagues and I have a strong case against Live Nation, and we will continue our lawsuit to protect consumers and restore fair competition to the live entertainment industry."

The trial had been underway for only one week when the settlement was announced, cutting short what legal observers expected would be months of testimony and evidence presentation. The quick resolution surprised the legal community and raised questions about the strength of the government's position going forward.

cards.headline: Scary Movie Tops Weekend Box Office as Masters of the Universe Opens Below Expectations
cards.teaser: The franchise returned for its first installment in 13 years and first with a Wayans director in 25 years.
cards.body:
Scary Movie led the weekend box office in its return to theaters after a 13-year absence. The comedy marked the first installment in the franchise in over a decade and the first with a Wayans family member directing in 25 years.

Amazon MGM Studios' Masters of the Universe stumbled in its opening weekend, falling short of box office expectations. The weekend represented a contrast between the successful return of an established comedy franchise and the disappointing debut of a major studio tentpole release.

cards.headline: Tom Holland Launches Film Format Challenge on Letterboxd for The Odyssey
cards.teaser: The platform will allow users to track and share the large format screens where they view Christopher Nolan's upcoming epic.
cards.body:
Tom Holland and Letterboxd introduced a new feature allowing users to document the large format screens where they watch films, starting with Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey. The initiative follows strong demand for premium format tickets to the upcoming epic.

For the first time on the platform, users can track and share the specific viewing formats they experience. The feature launches as fans secured advance tickets for The Odyssey in various premium formats including IMAX and other large screen presentations.

cards.headline: Documentary Examines Legacy of William Friedkin's Cruising
cards.teaser: Mineshaft: The Cruising Murders explores the 1980 thriller that was denounced by the queer community and later reclaimed as a portrait of a vanished social scene.
cards.body:
A new documentary probes the complex legacy of William Friedkin's 1980 erotic thriller Cruising. The film was long denounced by the queer community it claimed to represent but has been more recently reclaimed as a rare mainstream portrait of a social scene that no longer exists.

The documentary disentangles the film's onscreen achievements from its controversial reception and cultural impact. Cruising remains a film that means many different things to different audiences, making its legacy particularly complicated to assess decades after its release.

cards.headline: Tyne Daly Returns to Theater in Pasadena Playhouse's Brigadoon Revival
cards.teaser: The Cagney & Lacey star appears as the Widow Lundie, a role that received a gender switch from the original male character.
cards.body:
Tyne Daly stars in the acclaimed revival of Brigadoon now playing at Pasadena Playhouse. The actress appears as the Widow Lundie, a role that was gender-switched from the character's original incarnation as Mr. Lundie in earlier productions.

Daly serves as the marquee name in the production, though her stage time is limited compared to other cast members. The show features 68 cast and crew members, which Daly highlighted as representing live theater made by people rather than artificial intelligence.

cards.headline: Wonder Man Production Designers Detail Easter Eggs in Marvel Series
cards.teaser: The Disney+ show includes deep-cut Marvel Cinematic Universe references, from Simon's mutant ID to Asgard tourism posters.
cards.body:
Production designers Cindy Chao and Michele Yu detailed the Easter eggs hidden throughout Marvel's Wonder Man, now streaming on Disney+. The limited series features cameos and ties to the Marvel Cinematic Universe, with some references obvious and others requiring closer viewing to spot.

The show follows Yahya Abdul-Mateen II as Simon Williams and includes references ranging from a mutant ID belonging to the character to tourism posters for Asgard. The designers highlighted both prominent and subtle connections to the broader Marvel franchise woven into the production design.

cards.headline: Cheri Oteri's Zen Room Pilot to Screen at Dances with Films Festival
cards.teaser: The Saturday Night Live alum co-wrote and stars in the mockumentary-style workplace comedy set in the yoga and wellness world.
cards.body:
Cheri Oteri will screen her new pilot Zen Room at the Dances with Films festival. The Saturday Night Live alum co-wrote and stars in the mockumentary-style workplace comedy that takes aim at the yoga and wellness industry while celebrating its community.

The show is set within the yoga world and uses a workplace comedy format. Oteri currently appears in the new Scary Movie film that topped the weekend box office.

hero.headline: Medical schools agree to expand nutrition requirements
hero.teaser: Eight medical school accrediting organizations have agreed to increase nutrition education requirements across all levels of U.S. medical training.
hero.body:
The Department of Health and Human Services announced that numerous medical school accrediting organizations and assessors have agreed to increase nutrition requirements for U.S. medical education. The agreement affects education standards across multiple levels of training.

Eight medical school organizations signed on to the expanded requirements, which will apply to medical education, competency evaluation, training programs, and residency programs. The initiative is led by HHS under Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who has made nutrition education a priority.

cards.headline: Chief of staff Susie Wiles denies reported White House departure
cards.teaser: President Trump's chief of staff rejected a report that she plans to leave the White House after the midterm elections.
cards.body:
Susie Wiles, President Trump's chief of staff, rejected a Daily Mail report claiming she would leave the White House after the midterm elections. Wiles stated emphatically: "I am not going anywhere."

In her response, Wiles characterized the previous week as "accomplishment filled" for the Trump administration. As chief of staff, Wiles holds one of the most influential positions in the White House, overseeing the president's schedule and functioning as a key adviser and gatekeeper.

cards.headline: Katie Porter, Xavier Becerra lead California governor primary
cards.teaser: Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra and Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton are competing to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
California's governor primary is underway as Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra and Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton compete to replace Governor Gavin Newsom, who is not seeking reelection. Early results show Hilton and Becerra leading in the race.

California's top-two primary system places all candidates on a single ballot. The two candidates with the highest vote totals advance to the general election regardless of party affiliation.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. Her victory sets up a general election campaign where she could make history.

If elected in November, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in U.S. history. She advances to the general election as the Democratic nominee in a state that has leaned Democratic in recent statewide elections.

cards.headline: Spencer Pratt fails to make Los Angeles mayoral runoff
cards.teaser: President Trump's endorsed candidate for Los Angeles mayor appears unlikely to advance to the general election, prompting fraud claims from the president.
cards.body:
Spencer Pratt, President Trump's favored candidate for Los Angeles mayor, appears set to miss the runoff election as vote counting continues. Trump has responded to the results by making unsubstantiated claims of fraud in the race.

Votes are still being tallied in Los Angeles, where a large proportion of ballots are typically cast by mail. The delay in final results is customary for the city. Pratt's performance fell short of expectations, leaving him outside the top two positions needed to advance to the general election runoff.

cards.headline: Fewer Americans view democracy as central to national identity
cards.teaser: A new poll shows declining numbers of Americans consider democratically elected government essential to the country's identity ahead of its 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
Sixty-six percent of Americans said a democratically elected government is either extremely important or very important to U.S. identity, according to a new poll from The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research. The findings show a decline in how central Americans view democracy to national identity.

The poll was conducted ahead of the country's 250th birthday. The results suggest shifting attitudes about democratic governance and its role in defining American identity, though the survey did not provide comparison figures from previous years.

cards.headline: Trump to attend NBA Finals game in New York
cards.teaser: President Trump will attend Game 3 of the NBA Finals between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs at Madison Square Garden.
cards.body:
President Trump is scheduled to attend Game 3 of the NBA Finals between the New York Knicks and the San Antonio Spurs at Madison Square Garden on Monday evening. The game marks New York City's first NBA Finals game since 1999.

The president's attendance has prompted enhanced security measures across the venue. The NYPD and Secret Service cancelled the planned watch party outside Madison Square Garden, which had experienced disruptions during the previous game. The Knicks are urging fans to arrive at least two hours before tipoff and bring minimal belongings to accommodate security procedures.
